scope: Sample review, not a complete factual or spoken-audio audit

findings.note: Main scripts have clean spoken bodies, natural paragraph flow, and spoken dates. Hindi scripts use Devanagari consistently. No source URLs or stage instructions are mixed into the sampled narration.

Spoken script describes the research source and the reason not to invent a foundation story. Move research-process explanation to Sources or Basic_Info. Narration should directly introduce the documented pottery association and the cultural meaning of craftsmanship without inventing local techniques, dates or geography.

Spoken script mostly explains duplicate catalog labels and itinerary bookkeeping. Keep an alias note in structured data, then introduce the actual temple and locality naturally. One brief alternate-name sentence is enough for spoken content.
Narration correctly identifies Udaipur village in Vidisha Madhya Pradesh, rather than Udaipur Rajasthan.
Hindi narration correctly identifies Udaipur Machla Magra temple and separates it from Deshnoke.
Hindi narration marks the abandonment/curse account as folklore rather than established historical proof.
